extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians / graduate students working in complex analysis and geometric function theory (Krzyz conjecture, bounded nonvanishing functions)
extracted.subtask_description: A research-article style attempted proof of the Krzyz conjecture about sharp bounds for Taylor coefficients of bounded nonvanishing holomorphic functions in the unit disk; contains statements, lemmas and theorems relating extremal functions, Caratheodory class polynomials, and Riesz-Fejér factorization. (The paper is marked withdrawn due to an uncorrectable gap.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal notice / proof status
rubrics_metrics.description: The paper is marked WITHDRAWN: 'The proof contains an uncorrectable gap in the proof of theorem 7 on page 11.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Readers should treat the claimed proof and subsequent conclusions with caution; the document explicitly states it was withdrawn because of an uncorrectable gap in a key theorem. All subsequent derived claims may be invalid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carathéodory–Toeplitz criterion (Theorem 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A polynomial Q_n(z) = {h}_0 + sum_{k=1}^n {h}_k z^k can be extended to a function h(z)=Q_n(z)+o(z^n) in the Carathéodory class C (holomorphic with Re h > 0) iff the determinants M_k (defined in formula (4), Hermitian Toeplitz-type minors built from {h}_0,...,{h}_k) are either all positive or positive up to some index m ≤ n after which they all equal zero. In the latter (degenerate) case the extension is unique and h has the finite representation h(z)=sum_{k=1}^m α_k (1+e^{iφ_k} z)/(1-e^{iφ_k} z) with α_k>0 and 0≤φ_1<...<φ_m<2π.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a necessary-and-sufficient criterion to decide whether given initial coefficients arise from a Carathéodory-class function; the determinant conditions encode positivity. The uniqueness and finite-sum representation occur in the case of vanishing tail minors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of extremals in the Krzyz problem
rubrics_metrics.description: For fixed n, the maximum m_n := max_{f∈B} |{f}_n| is attained (extremal functions exist), since adding the zero function makes B compact in locally uniform topology and the n-th coefficient is continuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a compactness/continuity existence argument ensuring the Krzyz problem for fixed n has maximizers; used to justify studying boundary/coefficient-extremal properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of Bt functions (classification by t)
rubrics_metrics.description: For t>0, the subclass B_t of B with {f}_0 = e^{-t} is in bijection with the normalized Carathéodory class C_1 via f(z) = e^{-t} h(z) where h ∈ C_1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows reduction of problems on class B to problems about Carathéodory-class functions (positive real part) by factoring out the constant term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotation normalization for extremals
rubrics_metrics.description: Because B is invariant under rotations in z and w, when studying an extremal for index n one may assume without loss of generality that {f}_0>0 and {f}_n>0 (apply rotations in z-plane and w-plane).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard normalization reduces symmetry and fixes a canonical representative of an extremal for analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of extremal functions via Carathéodory representation (Corollary 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is extremal for index n (with {f}_0>0,{f}_n>0) and t=-ln{f}_0, then there exist α_k>0 and 0≤φ_1<...<φ_m<2π with m≤n and sum α_k = t such that f(z)=exp(- sum_{k=1}^m α_k (1+e^{iφ_k} z)/(1-e^{iφ_k} z) ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extremals correspond to exponentials of Carathéodory finite-sum functions; m≤n follows from the Carathéodory–Toeplitz degeneracy of minors for boundary points of the coefficient body.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-variation formula for coefficient under multiplicative perturbation (Lemma 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For v(z)=f(z)e^{-ε g(z)} with f,g holomorphic and ε→0 (real), the n-th Taylor coefficient satisfies {v}_n = {f}_n - ε {f·g}_n + o(ε).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the linearized change in the n-th coefficient under an internal multiplicative variation; used to derive necessary extremality inequalities (sign conditions) by considering admissible small ε variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extremal inequality for Carathéodory test functions (Theorem 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is extremal for index n then for any g ∈ C (Carathéodory class) one has Re({f}_n {g}_0 + {f}_{n-1}{g}_1 + ... + {f}_0 {g}_n) ≥ 0. In particular, for h=-ln f equality Re({f}_n {h}_0 + ... + {f}_0 {h}_n)=0 holds. The polynomial H(z) := {f}_n + 2{f}_{n-1} z + ... + 2{f}_0 z^n belongs to C and furthermore Re H(e^{iφ_k})=0 for φ_k appearing in the Carathéodory representation of h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived from admissible variations v=f e^{-ε g} and Lemma 1; provides linear constraints (supporting hyperplane type) satisfied by coefficients of extremal f relative to all Carathéodory test functions g. The polynomial H generated from f's coefficients also has positive real part and zeros of its real part at specified boundary points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence between vanishing linear form and zeros of Re H (Theorem 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For f=e^{-h} with h sum_{k=1}^m α_k (1+e^{iφ_k}z)/(1-e^{iφ_k}z) and g=sum_{k=1}^m β_k (1+e^{iφ_k}z)/(1-e^{iφ_k}z) (β_k>0), Re({f}_n{g}_0 + ... + {f}_0{g}_n)=0 iff Re H(e^{iφ_k})=0 for k=1,...,m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduces the linear extremal condition to pointwise vanishing of Re H at the finitely many angles φ_k via expansion and the positivity of H.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corollary identifying φ_k and m (Corollary 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a g built from n positive β_k and angles φ_k satisfies the extremal equality, then for an extremal f the representation f=exp(-sum_{k=1}^n α_k (1+e^{iφ_k}z)/(1-e^{iφ_k}z)) holds (i.e., m=n and the φ_k are the same).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular, for an extremal with the given g-test, all representation points φ_k are determined and equal in number to n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riesz–Fejér theorem for nonnegative trigonometric polynomials (Theorem 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: A real trigonometric polynomial T(φ)=a_0 + sum_{k=1}^n (a_k cos kφ - b_k sin kφ) that satisfies T(φ) ≥ 0 for all φ can be written as T(φ)=|P(e^{iφ})|^2 for some polynomial P(z)=sum_{k=0}^n p_k z^k whose zeros can be chosen outside the unit disk; P is unique up to a unimodular constant in that case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This factorization is used to pass from positivity of Re H on the circle to an analytic representation and is fundamental for counting roots and multiplicities (e.g., gives at most 2n real roots counting multiplicity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trigonometric restriction of Re H and root counting (Lemma 2 & Corollary 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: For H(z)=h_0 + 2 sum_{k=1}^n h_k z^k with h_0,a_k,b_k real-identifications, T(φ):=Re H(e^{iφ}) is a real trigonometric polynomial of degree n and if H∈C then T(φ)≥0 for all φ; a degree-n trigonometric polynomial has at most 2n roots on [0,2π) counting multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to deduce multiplicity properties of zeros of Re H and relate them to zeros of corresponding P in Riesz–Fejér factorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconstruction/uniqueness from harmonic real part (Theorems 5–7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any harmonic function g in the disk is the real part of a holomorphic function h, unique up to an additive imaginary constant; if two harmonic functions coincide on a set with an interior point they coincide identically; the Dirichlet problem for the disk admits unique harmonic solution for given continuous boundary data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These classical harmonic-analytic uniqueness and extension results justify passing from equality of Re H and Re Q on the unit circle to equality of analytic polynomials inside the disk (up to imaginary constant, fixed by normalization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation criterion for H ∈ C (Theorem 8)
rubrics_metrics.description: A polynomial H(z)=h_0 + 2 sum_{k=1}^n h_k z^k with h_0>0 has positive real part in Δ iff there exist complex numbers p_0,...,p_n (not all zero) such that h_k = sum_{j=0}^{n-k} p_{j+k}  ar p_j for k=0,...,n (i.e., Re H(e^{iφ}) = |P(e^{iφ})|^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives an explicit algebraic representation of the Carathéodory coefficients via convolution of coefficients of a polynomial P; this is the polynomial-level manifestation of Riesz–Fejér factorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness criteria for polynomials in Carathéodory class (Lemma 3 and Statements 1–2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If H∈C has form (17) and satisfies h_0 = 2|h_n|>0 then (up to rotation in z-plane) H(z)=h_0 (1 + η z^n) with |η|=1; equivalently, if H∈C, h_n>0 and all roots of H lie on ∂Δ then H(z)=h_0(1+z^n). Similarly, if the only roots of Re H are the n-th roots of -1 then H(z)=h_0(1+z^n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These characterize unique extremal-shaped polynomials in C with maximal relationship between h_0 and h_n and link location of (real-part) roots on the unit circle to the explicit H form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of extremal function under equality {f}_n = 2 {f}_0 (Theorem 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an extremal function f satisfies {f}_n = 2 {f}_0 > 0 then there is a unique such extremal and it equals F(z^n,1) (with F given by formula (1): F(z,t)=e^{-t}(1-z)/(1+z) specialized to t=1 and z->z^n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines Theorem 2, the characterization of H, and Carathéodory–Toeplitz minors to pin down the exact extremal function when this equality holds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Krzyz inequality and extremal characterization (Theorem 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: For every n∈N and f∈B one has |{f}_n| ≤ 2/e. Equality holds iff f(z)=e^{iθ} F(e^{iφ} z^n, 1) for some real θ,φ, where F is defined in formula (1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the stated main claim (the Krzyz conjecture): the sharp bound 2/e for the n-th coefficient and the classification of extremals. Note: the paper contains an editorial remark 'aError here: not F and −ln F should satisfy (10), but f and −ln F .' and the document is withdrawn due to a gap—so this final claim must be treated with caution.
